searchText: was checking https://light-sepolia.beaconcha.in/slot/11393482 as an example, and it seems that the requests from some LH nodes arrive much later into the slot which explains why I return a higher bid, it's a bit strange that the bn ask so late (500ms) into the slot? but playing timing games here got you some extra sepolia eth What intrigued me is that I send 6 requests from the 6 Charon nodes to the same Lighthouse BN at the same time and it returns different bids. I will check the BN logs today yeah just the timing due to delayed calls, eg. in the example above the lowest bid has 401ms into the slot while the highest was returned at 774ms are you returning 204 sometimes? I also see some requests get 204 and then lighthouse opts for the p2p bid (which is again from you) hmm seems like the 204 are because you requested a bid after you already published a block for same root/hash so I no longer serve a bid for that reasonable you know why there is a ~400ms difference when the requests are sent? are the nodes globally distributed? I found out that Lighthouse sends 1 request/CPU and I've devoted 4 CPUs to this machine, so it sends only 4 requests at the time. Meaning there are always 2 requests that are being sent (roughly) after the first 4 are replied > are the nodes globally distributed? the BN is on one machine, all the 6 DV nodes are on a separate second machine. Both under my desk though 🙂 lol why you need a whole cpu for a http request yeah... I won't contest that 😅 but it does explain why some are arriving 400ms late (waiting for the first ones to succeed) and then also why some are getting 204 (the ones that got served first were likely already used for a block to be proposed) the cpu is playing timing games but that's good testing my builder, so far it looks all as expected preparing for mainnet launch
